title: Speaker labels (who speaks when) from one mono recording
what_it_does: speakers.mjs labels who speaks when in a recording of two or more people on one track, locally and free with no account or token: sherpa-onnx offline diarization (pyannote-segmentation-3.0 + CAM++ speaker embedding). Writes {speakers:["A","B"], turns:[{start,end,speaker}], words?:[{w,start,end,speaker}], summary}; with a transcribe-local words file every word gets the speaker whose turn covers its midpoint.
when_to_use: Podcasts and interviews recorded on one microphone/track, when the video should show who is talking (speaker cards, captions in two colours, per-speaker cuts). Not needed for a single speaker, and not for multi-channel recordings (use the channel). Labels are A, B... in order of first speech; the person maps them to names. Always have a human listen to a few handovers before trusting them.
needs: python3 (3.9+, with the venv module); `node parts/speakers/speakers.mjs --install` makes a private venv in ~/.cache/create-video-engine/speakers/ and pip-installs sherpa-onnx (Apache-2.0) and numpy there, no root

two ONNX models downloaded once from github.com/k2-fsa/sherpa-onnx releases, sha-256 checked: pyannote-segmentation-3.0 (MIT, ~7 MB) and 3D-Speaker CAM++ zh_en (Apache-2.0, ~28 MB), cached in the same folder
notes: Free local default; pyannote's own gated pipeline (Hugging Face token) is deliberately not used. Install footprint about 120 MB (wheels ~30 MB + onnxruntime, models ~35 MB). Speed on an 8 GB M1: 28 min of audio in about 4 min. Same-voice-type cases (two men, one phone mic, outdoor noise) are the weak spot; it cannot label overlapping speech separately beyond what the segmentation model resolves.
